canonical.title: Kruskal's Algorithm — Minimum Spanning Tree Weight

narrative.title: Sorting the Lease Bids into a Grid
narrative.scenario: A satellite operator leases ground-station links from bids, each bid quoting one link at a price. The accountant sorts every bid cheapest-first and buys it unless both ends already connect through previously bought links — buying only links that merge two separate station groups, never one that closes a private loop. When every station belongs to one group, the bill is the minimum leasing cost.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n (vertices 0..n-1) and an edge list edges where [u, v, w] is an undirected link of cost w.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the total weight of the minimum spanning tree.
constraints: The graph is connected and undirected

testCases.explanation: Sorted bids buy 1 then 3, connecting everything for 4; the 5 bid is skipped.
The 1, 2, 3 chain wins again; the 4-bid would close a loop and is refused.

hintLevels: Level 1: Cheapest links first — a link is refused only when it would close a loop.
Level 2: A union-find answers 'already connected?' in near-constant time; buy the link and union when not.
Level 3: Exactly n-1 purchases connect n stations; stop early once the count is reached.
